title: Tensor with a constant complex over $\mathbf Z$
statement:
Let $X$ be a
quasi-compact and
quasi-separated scheme. For $E\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ and
$K\in\Dplus(\mathbf Z)$, the canonical map

$$
\RGamma(X_{\Et},E)\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}K\longrightarrow
\RGamma\bigl(X_{\Et},E\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}\underline{K}\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Write $R=R\Gamma(X_{\Et},-)$ and $a^*K=\underline K$. The canonical map is precisely the counit mate $\alpha_{E,K}:RE\otimes^L K\to R(E\otimes^L a^*K)$ of [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] to the ringed-topos morphism from the small etale topos to the one-point topos, with coefficient ring $\mathbf Z$. This gives exact functors of K, a natural comparison commuting with the triangle connecting maps, and $\alpha_{E,\mathbf Z}=1_{RE}$. In the E variable, the same counit formula also commutes with cones: for a chain map u the cone differential is the matrix $(d,u;0,-d)$, tensor distributes over its two summands, and naturality with u gives the off-diagonal square, with the same minus sign on both shifted summands. Applying the triangulated functor R gives a morphism of these cone triangles. Thus the isomorphism property is stable under shifts and finite extensions in either variable.

proof.text: We will use the lower-bound fact $C\in D^{\ge c}\Rightarrow RC\in D^{\ge c}$. Indeed global sections is the additive right adjoint of the constant-sheaf functor, hence left exact, and abelian etale sheaves form a Grothendieck category. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-truncation-iso] to $0\to C$ and $n=c-1$: the cohomology maps are isomorphisms in degrees at most $c-1$, and the degree-c map from zero is a monomorphism. Hence $H^j(RC)=0$ for $j<c$. The standard t-structure supplies a representative of RC zero below c.

source.place: Tag 0F0E (lemma-pull-out-constant), lower-bound vanishing used with the stupid truncation triangles

proof.text: Let $P$ be a bounded-below complex of flat abelian groups and choose an integer $b$ with $P^i=0$ for $i<b$. Each $P^i$ is torsion free: tensor the injection $\mathbf Z\xrightarrow{m}\mathbf Z$ with $P^i$ for each nonzero integer m. Every subgroup, in particular $\ker(d_P^j)$, is then torsion free, hence flat by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat] with $A=\mathbf Z$. Thus every good truncation $\tau_{\le j}P$ is bounded and flat. Constant sheaves are exact, preserve flat objects and, as left adjoint to global sections, preserve colimits; hence their termwise images are also bounded flat complexes, and $\underline P=\operatorname{colim}_{j\ge b}\underline{\tau_{\le j}P}$, degreewise. The same colimit formula holds for $P$ itself. Apply [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] on the etale site and on the one-point site to each of these bounded truncations. For any acyclic complex $A$, [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor] identifies its tensor with the colimit complex with the filtered colimit of its tensors with these truncations; exactness of filtered colimits, also in that cited statement, makes this colimit of acyclic complexes acyclic. This proves K-flatness of $P$ and of its constant complex directly from the definition. It applies in particular to every stupid tail or head of $P$, since those still have flat terms and are bounded below.

source.place: Tag 0F0E (lemma-pull-out-constant), justification that ordinary total tensor with the flat integer model computes derived tensor; via good truncations and the existing K-flatness/colimit criteria

proof.text: First let E be an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ in degree zero and let K be a flat abelian group M in degree zero. By [lem-kun-lazard-flat-module], choose a small directed presentation $M=\operatorname{colim}_i F_i$ by finite free groups. Constant sheaves preserve this colimit because they are left adjoint to global sections; tensoring sheaves with $\mathcal F$ preserves it by [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor]. The qcqs hypothesis on X permits [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-filtered-colimit], so for $q\ge0$ we have $H^q(X,\mathcal F\otimes\underline M)=\operatorname{colim}_i H^q(X,\mathcal F\otimes\underline{F_i})$. On the source side [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-derived-tensor], with $R=A=\mathbf Z$, identifies $H^q(R\mathcal F\otimes^L M)$ with $\operatorname{colim}_iH^q(R\mathcal F\otimes^L F_i)$. For $F_i=\mathbf Z^{r_i}$, both sides and the comparison are the finite direct sum of $\alpha_{\mathcal F,\mathbf Z}$, which is the identity by step 1. Naturality identifies the two directed systems of comparison maps, so their colimit is an isomorphism. Flatness and the K-flatness calculation of step 3 identify the derived tensor on the right with $\mathcal F\otimes\underline M$. Both sides vanish in negative degrees by step 2, so this proves the derived comparison for this case.

source.place: Tag 0F0E (lemma-pull-out-constant), Lazard and Theorem colimit (Tag 0739), final paragraph

proof.text: Keep K=M[0] flat and now let E be arbitrary bounded below. Flatness means that tensor preserves the kernel-image short exact sequences of a complex, whence $H^i(C\otimes M)=H^i(C)\otimes M$; the same holds for $\underline M$ on sheaves, since constant sheaves preserve flat objects. Fix n and put $E_n=\tau_{\le n}E$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-truncation-iso], $RE_n\to RE$ induces an isomorphism on $H^n$. Exact flat tensor gives the same for the source comparisons, and $E_n\otimes\underline M\to E\otimes\underline M$ has isomorphic cohomology through n and a monomorphism in degree n+1; the same cited truncation lemma gives the target isomorphism in degree n. The object E_n has cohomology in only finitely many degrees. Starting with its lowest nonzero cohomology sheaf, successively use the canonical triangles $\tau_{\le j-1}E_n\to\tau_{\le j}E_n\to H^j(E_n)[-j]\to$ from [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle]. Step 4 handles each sheaf, shifts are handled by step 1, and the long exact cohomology sequences of the morphisms of triangles propagate the isomorphism by the five lemma. This proves the comparison for E_n and hence in degree n for E. Since n was arbitrary, it proves the flat-group case for every E.

proof.text: For fixed E, let P be a bounded complex of flat abelian groups. Induct on the number of its potentially nonzero terms. The zero complex is immediate; a single term is a shift of the flat-group case of step 5. For a complex supported in [b,N], the degreewise split short exact sequence $0\to\sigma_{\ge b+1}P\to P\to P^b[-b]\to0$ gives the stupid truncation triangle. Step 1 turns the comparison into a morphism of triangles. The first and third comparisons are isomorphisms by induction and step 5; exactness of the cohomology sequences gives the middle isomorphism. This establishes all bounded flat coefficient complexes.

source.place: Tag 0F0E (lemma-pull-out-constant), bounded flat complexes reduced to single flat modules by stupid truncation triangles

proof.text: For general K use [lem-kun-torsionfree-complex-model] to choose a flat complex P representing K with $P^i=0$ for $i<b$. Choose a representative $\mathcal E$ of E with $\mathcal E^i=0$ for $i<a$. By the K-flatness calculation of step 3, P, all its stupid tails, and their termwise constant complexes are K-flat; thus ordinary total tensors with them compute the derived tensors. Fix n and choose $N\ge\max(b,n-a+1)$. Put $T=\sigma_{\ge N+1}P$ and $B=\sigma_{\le N}P$. The complexes $\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal E\otimes\underline T)$ and $\operatorname{Tot}(RE\otimes T)$ are zero below $a+N+1\ge n+2$, where the latter uses the lower-bounded representative of RE from step 2. Step 2 gives the same vanishing below n+2 after applying R to the former. Apply both functors of step 1 to the triangle $T\to P\to B\to T[1]$. The vanishing of both degree n and degree n+1 of each tail shows that the maps from the P terms to the B terms induce isomorphisms on $H^n$. Step 6 proves that the comparison for the bounded flat complex B is an isomorphism. The natural square therefore proves $H^n(\alpha_{E,K})$ is an isomorphism. This holds for every integer n, so $\alpha_{E,K}$ is an isomorphism in the derived category.
